theme.title: NBA Mix 60
theme.subtitle: Five moments from across NBA history
theme.recap: Five NBA stories, five different numbers: a quick tour of stars, teams, records and surprises.

questions.prompt: Away from the corners, how far is the NBA three-point arc from the center of the basket, in feet?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: in the National Basketball Association (NBA) the arc is 23 feet 9 inches (7.24 m) from the center of the basket

funFacts.text: The three-point rule debuted in the short-lived American Basketball League before the NBA ever adopted it.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the newly formed American Basketball League (ABL) became the first basketball league to institute the rule in 1961

funFacts.text: The ABA paired three-pointers with dunks in its marketing to offer fans a different kind of basketball.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: During the 1970s, the ABA used the three-point shot, along with the slam dunk, as a marketing tool to compete with the NBA

funFacts.text: The NBA introduced the arc on a trial basis in 1979; Boston's Chris Ford made the league's first official three.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Chris Ford of the Boston Celtics is credited with making the first three-point shot in NBA history on October 12, 1979

questions.prompt: How many consecutive games did Phoenix win during December in its Barkley MVP season?
questions.note: 14 straight wins during an undefeated month.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: posted a 14-game winning streak in December; the team posted a 14–0 record that month

funFacts.text: Phoenix started 7–4 before the team caught fire in December.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Suns got off to a 7–4 start to the regular season

funFacts.text: The Suns reached the All-Star break at 38–10.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: held a 38–10 record at the All-Star break

funFacts.text: Another 11-game winning streak came between March and April.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: posted an 11-game winning streak between March and April

questions.prompt: How many regular-season games did the 2022–23 Heat win before reaching the Finals?
questions.note: 44–38, then a run to the Finals as an eighth seed.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: They regressed from their 53–29 record the previous season and finished with a record of 44–38

funFacts.text: Miami had to survive the play-in tournament to reach the postseason despite finishing seventh in the East.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Miami had to go through two play-in games to extend their season

funFacts.text: The Heat entered the playoffs with the league's worst scoring average and a negative point differential.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the only team in the league to qualify for the playoffs with a negative point differential

funFacts.text: Undrafted players including Caleb Martin and Gabe Vincent supplied vital production around the established stars.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: undrafted players such as Martin, Gabe Vincent, Duncan Robinson, and Max Strus

questions.prompt: How many free throws did Wilt Chamberlain attempt in 1966–67?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: his 875 free throw attempts

funFacts.text: Wilt hit a league-record share of his field-goal attempts as his offense shifted toward efficiency.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Shooting less, he made a league-record 68% of his shots

funFacts.text: Even as he shot less frequently, Wilt still led the league in rebounds that season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: while scoring 24 points per game and once again leading the NBA in rebounds

funFacts.text: The league named Wilt its regular-season MVP in the same year Philadelphia captured the title.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Wilt Chamberlain, NBA Most Valuable Player Award

questions.prompt: How many points did Derrick Rose score in Game 3 against Atlanta in the 2011 playoffs?
questions.note: 44 points, a career high at the time in Chicago's road win.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Derrick Rose scored a career high 44 pts vs the Atlanta Hawks on May 6, 2011.

funFacts.text: Chicago won the game in Atlanta and took control of a competitive second-round series.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: May 6 @ Atlanta W 99–82

funFacts.text: The Bulls ultimately eliminated Atlanta in six games to reach the Eastern Conference finals.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: defeated the Atlanta Hawks in six games in the semifinals

funFacts.text: Miami's LeBron James, Dwyane Wade and Chris Bosh later ended Chicago's playoff run.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: eliminated by the Miami Heat team led by LeBron James, Dwyane Wade, and Chris Bosh
